# Web & development notes development notes

> WebView, JavaScript bridges, mini programs, blog maintenance and development reflections.

## Historical context

Historical development notes from 2015–2017. Their original publication dates and source attribution are retained; translation or catalog updates do not make the examples current.
The examples were not rerun for this reorganization. Old Swift syntax, APIs, dependencies, service addresses and App Store rules may be obsolete; check current official documentation before applying them.

## Articles by original publication date

- [Using UIWebView: techniques and notes](https://allluckly.cn/en/journal/2015-07-17-using-uiwebview-techniques-and-notes/index.md): Collects common UIWebView settings for loading web pages inside a native interface, including transparent backgrounds, scaling, phone-number detection and JavaScript interaction. It also discusses the layout and communication costs of a cross-platform approach. Originally published: 2015-07-17. Uses UIWebView APIs and is retained as a historical implementation record. Originally credited to Bison. Content is retained as published.
- [A technical blog can be more than a website](https://allluckly.cn/en/journal/2015-11-28-a-technical-blog-can-be-more-than-a-website/index.md): Records an experiment in wrapping a personal technical blog as an iOS app. UIWebView displays the home and category pages and handles loading callbacks, while search and interaction-stutter issues remain documented as unresolved at the time. Originally published: 2015-11-28. Published in 2015. The website wrapper uses UIWebView. Originally credited to Bison. Content is retained as published.
- [Helping Baidu discover a GitHub Pages blog: a historical workflow](https://allluckly.cn/en/journal/2015-12-27-helping-baidu-discover-a-github-pages-blog-a-historical-workflow/index.md): Records mirroring a GitHub Pages blog to GitCafe Pages, using SourceTree to clone and push branches, bind a domain and configure regional DNS. The workflow aimed to improve access and search indexing in mainland China at the time. Originally published: 2015-12-27. Published in 2015. The workflow depends on the GitCafe Pages service and search-indexing conditions of that period. Originally credited to Bison. Content is retained as published.
- [A beginner developer's review of 2015](https://allluckly.cn/en/journal/2016-02-01-a-beginner-developer-s-review-of-2015/index.md): Reflects on the author's job search, development projects and self-directed learning in 2015. Starting a technical blog, learning Swift, releasing open-source UI components and meeting other developers provide the personal context for this early stage of growth. Originally published: 2016-02-01. Originally credited to Bison. Content is retained as published.
- [JavaScript and Native iOS Interaction with JavaScriptCore](https://allluckly.cn/en/journal/2016-07-05-javascript-and-native-ios-interaction-with-javascriptcore/index.md): Compares early UIWebView URL interception with JavaScriptCore. Using JSContext, it introduces executing JavaScript from native code, registering native methods, and passing data between the two environments. Originally published: 2016-07-05. The article is organized around the introduction of JavaScriptCore in iOS 7 and uses the WebView interaction approaches of that period. Originally credited to Sindri; edited and archived by Bison.
- [Setting Up React Native for iOS Development on a Mac](https://allluckly.cn/en/journal/2016-07-27-setting-up-react-native-for-ios-development-on-a-mac/index.md): Records a React Native setup on macOS: installing Homebrew, Node.js, watchman, and flow, creating a project, opening the iOS project, and refreshing code in the simulator. Originally published: 2016-07-27. Published in 2016, the article uses index.ios.js and the React Native project initialization workflow available at the time. Originally credited to Bison. Content is retained as published.
- [WeChat Mini Programs from Scratch, Part 1](https://allluckly.cn/en/journal/2016-10-17-wechat-mini-programs-from-scratch-part-1/index.md): Builds an IT Blog mini program from an iOS developer's perspective. It explains the roles of app.json, app.js, WXML, and WXSS, configures a TabBar, and uses templates and list rendering to display article data. Originally published: 2016-10-17. Published in October 2016, the article explicitly dates from the WeChat Mini Programs closed beta. Originally credited to Bison. Content is retained as published.
- [WeChat Mini Programs from Scratch, Part 2](https://allluckly.cn/en/journal/2016-10-18-wechat-mini-programs-from-scratch-part-2/index.md): Adds an article detail page to the existing list, using navigator for navigation and parameters. It then adjusts spacing, image placement, and text layout in WXSS to refine the list into the intended page design. Originally published: 2016-10-18. This installment was written during the WeChat Mini Programs closed beta in 2016. Originally credited to Bison. Content is retained as published.
- [WeChat Mini Programs from Scratch, Part 3](https://allluckly.cn/en/journal/2016-10-19-wechat-mini-programs-from-scratch-part-3/index.md): Connects an article list to a network request, reads the response, updates the page with setData, and adjusts WXML field bindings. It also records the limitations encountered at the time with image URLs and HTML5 detail pages. Originally published: 2016-10-19. This implementation was recorded during the 2016 closed beta. Its image and HTML5 display issues describe only the author's attempts at that time. Originally credited to Bison. Content is retained as published.
